It makes the PR much smaller!

So with routerboard routers, it fetches successfully the device info.

@engrbm87 Would it be ok if I do that instead 🔼 ?

Here are the rationals behind it:

It triggers the autodetection the first time it tries to get some device info.
During the autodetection, it silences protocols errors as they are expected for non routerboard routers.
It won't silence any protocol errors outside of the autodetection.

```python
if self.is_routerboard is None:
  self.is_routerboard = self.detect_routerboard_router()
```

I kept this in the `get_info` method as this method is also called from `update_devices` ([source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mikrotik/hub.py#L134)). But I can move it to `get_hub_details` as we are sure that `get_hub_details` will be called before `update_devices`

([source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mikrotik/__init__.py#L27))
```python
    await hass.async_add_executor_job(coordinator.api.get_hub_details)

```

CHR is RouterOS but meant to be run in a VM ([source](https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/display/ROS/Cloud+Hosted+Router%2C+CHR)). I used qemu to run a CHR router and make some tests. On my Mikrotik physical router: On the CHR router: The differences in /: My phycial router has the additional commands: caps-man, partitions, zerotier and blink The differences in /system: My physical router has the additional command: routerboard The CHR router has the additionals commands: hardware, ups, check-disk The `hardware` command looked promising but it displays nothing useful: ``` [admin@MikroTik] > /system/hardware/print multi-cpu: yes ``` For the software version, we could use `/system/packages` and return the version of the "routeros" package. ``` [admin@MikroTik] > /system/package/print Columns: NAME, VERSION # NAME VERSION 0 routeros 7.13 ``` What do you think?

Also if you want to play with a CHR router, you can download the raw disk image [here](https://mikrotik.com/download#chr) and run the VM with qemu with this command:

```
qemu-system-x86_64 --serial stdio -drive format=raw,file=chr-7.13.img
```

Hi @amigthea, From what I see in the integration's code, it tries to get some info about the router by using the following commands: - `/system/identity/getall` - `/system/routerboard/getall` - `/caps-man/interface/print` - `/interface/wireless/print` Can you check if you can run the other commands in your router's terminal? (Note: I think you'll need to replace `getall` by `print`) When you are under `/system` and you hit TAB what do you see? On my Mikrotik routerboard I have this : On yours, do you see something that seems to replace the `routerboard` command? I'm trying to find out if we can use another command to get the same kind of information than with `/system/routerboard/getall` or if we should just find a way to disable the retrieval of those info for Mikrotik CHR. As `/system/routerboard/getall` is only used to get the model, firmware and serial number. It should not matter that much if those info are empty/missing.

Hi @CedricFinance and thank you for joining the discussion,
Of all those four commands only the last two are executed (exist) on routeros version 7.6, both of the CHR version and routerboard (physical) version of the operative system.

If I replace `getall` with `print` all four commands works on the routerboard version of the os. But, as expected, the command `/system/routerboard` do not exist at all on the CHR version, so that's the error is coming from.

The /system menu on the CHR version doesn't seems to have a `/system/routerboard` replacement because, I suppose, it's a virtualized version of the operative system and that command display only hardware related infos like serial-number, firmware, model etc as you came up to too

>Of all those four commands only the last two are executed (exist) on routeros version 7.6, both of the CHR version and routerboard (physical) version of the operative system.

It's because the four commands are API commands. They can differ slightly from terminal commands.

To solve the issue with CHR, I see 3 main ways:
1. Ask the type of router in the UI and if it's CHR, the integration will not try to get the routerboard infos
2. Try to get the routerboard info and if it fails to, remember it and don't retry (until homeassistant is restarted)
3. Find a way to detect the type of Mikrotik device and react accordingly (but right now, I don't know how to do it)

The 1. solution is maybe a bit better but a bit more complicated.
The 2. solution is easy but you'll have the log once after every HA restart.
I don't see how I could do the 3. solution, so I'm open if you have any ideas.

What do you think?
Thank you for the insight of the API commands difference, I wasn't aware of that. I agree, the 1.solution is the most straightforward and clean, I would prefear it too
Ok. I'll learn how to do the first solution.

Suppressing a warning for an integration is simple. Just change the logging level for this integration to `Error` or above.
```yaml 
logger:
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.mikrotik: error
```
